archetype.name: Dual-Threat (scramble-first)
archetype.definition: An undrafted, 6-foot rookie backup whose passing is built on short, safe throws and whose real value comes when the pocket breaks down and he runs for first downs.

report.headline: A scrambler holding the fort, not yet a passer who can carry an offense.
report.take:
Jalon Daniels is Tampa Bay's undrafted rookie QB2, and his season is a three-start audition (Weeks 4-6) plus two cameo appearances behind Baker Mayfield. Those starts went 1-2, and the passing line is about what you'd expect from an emergency starter. He averages 5.11 yards per attempt, 50th of 54 qualifiers. His adjusted net yards per dropback (3.77) sits 2.73 below the league average, and his interception rate (5.1%) also ranks 50th. The Bucs plainly scaled the playbook down for him. His intended air yards are 5.23, he throws 4.15 yards short of the sticks on average, and 25 of his 98 attempts were behind the line of scrimmage. This was a team with the No. 2 defense in the league asking its backup not to lose the game.

The legs are what make the profile work. He scrambled on 13% of his dropbacks: 16 scrambles for 119 yards, 7 first downs and +0.382 EPA each, which is far better than anything he did through the air. His 123 rushing yards rank 13th among QBs despite three starts. His rush EPA per carry of 0.281 is the one clearly positive number in the dossier. The pressure numbers fit the same picture. He was pressured on 25.2% of dropbacks and took sacks on a third of those, which is the usual cost of a quarterback who looks to escape rather than hang in and throw. The scrambles roughly pay for that trade, but he hasn't yet turned extended plays into completions downfield.

The passing problem sits in the middle of the field. On throws of 10-19 air yards he completed 26.3% with a CPOE of -29 and two interceptions. In one-score fourth quarters he was at -0.479 EPA per play with three picks. His 18.4% bad-throw rate ranks 39th of 42, so this is accuracy, not just drops. His connection with Emeka Egbuka was the biggest single drain: 29 targets at -0.431 EPA each. Meanwhile Ted Hurst, Cade Otton and Chris Godwin were all positive. The nine deep attempts (+0.812 EPA) and nine red-zone attempts (three TDs) look good but are too few to lean on. The game log tells the same split story. He was efficient against Dallas (+4.8 EPA, against the defense now ranked 32nd) and fell apart against Pittsburgh (22/43, five sacks, -18 EPA).

Where it goes depends entirely on Mayfield's foot. Mayfield is questionable for Week 11 at Detroit with a sprain, and his expected return date is game day. If Daniels starts, he gets the friendliest passing matchup on the schedule. Even then, the realistic version is a run-and-scramble game plan with throws underneath to Otton and the backs, not a breakout as a passer.

strengths.title: Scrambles that move the chains
strengths.body: He leaves the pocket often and it pays: 16 scrambles produced 7 first downs at +0.382 EPA per scramble, far above his per-dropback passing value. This comes from his athleticism and a willingness to bail early, and it is the most repeatable part of his game. It gives him a fantasy floor even when the passing stalls.

strengths.title: Rushing volume as a starter
strengths.body: He averaged 39 rushing yards in his three starts and ranks 13th among QBs in rushing yards despite limited snaps. Tampa Bay's run game is a strength (9th in rushing EPA), so the offense naturally leans on the ground with him. That lasts as long as he's starting.

strengths.title: Red-zone and deep flashes
strengths.body: Inside the 20 he has three TDs on nine attempts with a +13.1 CPOE. On the nine throws of 20+ air yards he posted +0.812 EPA per play. Both are hints of real arm talent and touch, but at nine attempts each they are glimpses that will regress, not established skills.

concerns.title: Intermediate throws are broken
concerns.body: Between 10 and 19 air yards he completed 26.3% with a -29 CPOE and two interceptions, the main reason his yards per attempt ranks 50th. His 18.4% bad-throw rate says the misses are on him, not on his receivers. It also explains why the staff kept his targets so short: until he can hit the middle tier, defenses can squat underneath.

concerns.title: Turnovers when games tighten
concerns.body: In one-score fourth quarters he was at -0.479 EPA per play with three interceptions and a 40.9% completion rate. His 5.1% interception rate ranks 50th of 54. That's a big problem for a team whose defense keeps games close and needs its quarterback simply to not give the ball away. Some of it is rookie decision-making that can improve, but it is the biggest risk if he starts again.

concerns.title: No rapport with Egbuka
concerns.body: His most-targeted receiver produced -0.431 EPA per target on 29 targets. Godwin, Otton and Hurst were all positive with him. Feeding the top read without the timing to hit him sank drives, and the target mix might shift toward the tight end and Hurst in a future start.

trend.note: His three starts swung from a clean win at Dallas (+4.8 EPA against the league's worst defense) to a 43-attempt, five-sack, -18 EPA loss to Pittsburgh. Since then he has been a backup, so his last-three window covers effectively two starts and is too thin to call a trend.

nextGame.headline: If Mayfield sits, a short-handed Lions defense invites him to throw
nextGame.body:
Detroit is the kind of defense his profile needs, at least on paper. It ranks 24th in pass EPA and 27th against short throws, and it allows quarterbacks 20.8 PPR points and 281.2 yards a game, both 31st. Offenses pass against it more than almost anyone, and its tight-end defense ranks 31st. The weak spots line up with his underneath game and with Cade Otton. The catch is the pass rush, which ranks 5th in hit rate and 4th in sack rate, against a quarterback who takes sacks on a third of his pressures. Detroit's offense (5th in pass EPA) and the 6.5-point spread point to Tampa Bay trailing and throwing more than it would like. That adds volume but also more chances for the late-game mistakes that have hurt him.

Availability drives everything. Mayfield is questionable with a foot sprain and his estimated return is game day. Daniels only has value if Mayfield is ruled out, so watch the late-week reports. On the Lions' side, the losses matter directly. Aidan Hutchinson's torn ACL removes their best edge rusher and softens that sack threat. D.J. Reed and Kerby Joseph are out, which thins the secondary, and LB Jack Campbell is on IR, which weakens coverage over the middle. The game is indoors, so weather is not a factor.

keyMatchups.title: Otton against a leaky middle
keyMatchups.body: Detroit gives up +0.69 EPA per target to opposing top tight ends, 31st in the league. Otton was positive with Daniels at +0.235 per target. With Campbell on IR and Joseph out, the short middle is the easiest throw on the board for a quarterback who lives under 10 air yards.

keyMatchups.title: Pass rush minus Hutchinson
keyMatchups.body: Detroit's 4th-ranked sack rate was built largely with Hutchinson, who is now out for the season. Daniels converts pressure into sacks at a 33.3% rate, so a weaker rush gives him more room to escape and scramble rather than go down.

keyMatchups.title: Game script forces his arm
keyMatchups.body: Detroit runs a top-five pass offense, and Tampa Bay is a 6.5-point underdog with a run-heavy identity (-7.5 pass rate over expected). Detroit's run defense ranks 8th, so if the Bucs fall behind, he'll have to throw into the intermediate range where he has struggled most.

nextGame.watch: Mayfield's status first. If Daniels starts, watch whether he completes anything in the 10-19 yard range or lives entirely on checkdowns and scrambles.

restOfSeason.body:
As long as Mayfield is healthy, Daniels is a backup with cameo snaps and no fantasy value. The projections below are per start, for any game Mayfield misses. In those games, expect a run-first plan built on scrambles and throws underneath. Something like 140-195 passing yards and 25-45 rushing yards is realistic, with interceptions remaining a steady risk.

The rushing value is sustainable: it comes from who he is, and it held up across all three starts. The red-zone TD rate and the deep-ball efficiency will cool, since each rests on only nine throws. The interception rate should come down somewhat from its current bottom-five level as he gets more reps, but not to league average without real progress on intermediate accuracy. A soft opponent like Detroit raises the ceiling for one week. It doesn't change what he is.
swingFactors: How long Mayfield's foot sprain keeps him out
Whether he can hit the 10-19 yard window
Game script forcing the run-heavy Bucs to throw

confidence.note: Three starts, no career history, and his role depends on Mayfield's health.
